title: Wall Street Faces a Pivotal Week After the AI-Led Selloff
content:
U.S. investors entered November facing a crowded calendar of corporate earnings, economic releases and the November 3 midterm elections. The immediate backdrop was a sharp Friday decline: the S&P 500 fell 1.8%, the Nasdaq Composite lost 2.9% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 1.1%, according to the Associated Press. Technology and artificial-intelligence shares led the retreat.

The selloff followed results from major technology companies that revived questions about how quickly heavy data-center and AI infrastructure spending can generate profits. Investors are now looking beyond headline revenue growth and asking companies to explain capital expenditure, cash flow, customer demand and expected returns.

Apple and Palantir are among the companies scheduled to report Monday, with AMD and other large firms due later in the week. The October employment report is also expected Friday. These events could either reassure investors that earnings and economic growth remain resilient or reinforce concerns about valuations and spending.

The week's market direction is not predetermined. Earnings guidance, labor-market data and election-related policy expectations may each move prices, and investors should distinguish reported results from forecasts and analyst expectations.

Source: Associated Press, November 2, 2026 — https://apnews.com/article/048328e49e47ce7afe6c1fb9d9acf13d

title: AI Spending Becomes Wall Street's Biggest Test of Big Tech Cash Flow
content:
The latest technology-stock weakness has focused attention on a difficult question for large technology companies: how much cash can they invest in artificial intelligence before shareholders demand clearer evidence of returns? Recent earnings from Alphabet and Amazon intensified that debate as investors weighed infrastructure commitments against cash generation.

Building AI capacity requires data centers, advanced processors, networking equipment, electricity and long-term supply agreements. Those investments may support future services and cloud revenue, but the costs arrive before every new product or workload has proved commercially successful. A company can report rising sales while free cash flow comes under pressure because capital spending is accelerating even faster.

Reuters reported that Goldman Sachs expects hyperscaler capital expenditure to reach about $800 billion this year and $1.2 trillion in 2027. Those figures illustrate the scale of the investment cycle, not a guarantee that spending will produce equivalent profits.

Investors are likely to examine management commentary on utilization, customer commitments, depreciation and monetization. The key issue is not whether AI demand exists, but whether revenue and productivity gains can justify the enormous cost of building capacity.

Source: Reuters, November 2, 2026 — https://www.reuters.com/world/china/global-markets-global-markets-2026-11-02/

title: Intel's Sharp Decline Highlights a More Selective Market for AI Chip Stocks
content:
Semiconductor shares have become more sensitive to company-specific forecasts as investors reassess the artificial-intelligence trade. Intel fell nearly 29% on Friday after its latest report and outlook disappointed investors, contributing to a broader technology-led decline on Wall Street.

The reaction shows that exposure to the chip industry is no longer enough to guarantee investor enthusiasm. Markets are comparing product road maps, manufacturing execution, customer demand, margins and the ability to convert large investment programs into sustainable cash flow. Companies associated with AI infrastructure can still fall sharply when guidance fails to meet high expectations.

The pressure also reflects the difference between demand for AI computing and the financial performance of each supplier. Data-center operators may continue spending while individual chipmakers face product delays, competition, pricing pressure or execution challenges.

Investors will have another important reference point when AMD reports later in the week. Its results and outlook may help clarify whether demand remains broad across processors and accelerators, but one company's report cannot determine the prospects of the entire semiconductor sector.

Source: Reuters, November 1, 2026 — https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/midterm-us-elections-earnings-jobs-data-loom-for-aiwary-stock-market-4920345

title: Apple Earnings Put iPhone Demand and AI Monetization in Focus
content:
Apple's scheduled results on Monday are arriving at a sensitive moment for the technology sector. Investors will be looking for updates on iPhone demand, services growth, margins and the company's ability to translate new technology features into products customers are willing to buy.

Reuters reported that Apple is expected to post quarterly earnings per share of about $2 on revenue of roughly $113 billion. These are market expectations, not reported results. The company's commentary on demand for its latest iPhone generation and its outlook for the holiday shopping period may matter as much as the headline quarterly figures.

Apple is also being watched as investors debate whether artificial-intelligence features can create a meaningful upgrade cycle. The commercial impact may depend on how quickly new capabilities reach customers, whether they improve the user experience and how they affect hardware replacement decisions.

The report will be assessed against elevated expectations and a volatile market backdrop. Investors should compare actual results with the company's own guidance and avoid treating analyst forecasts as guaranteed outcomes.

Source: Reuters, November 2, 2026 — https://www.reuters.com/world/china/global-markets-global-markets-2026-11-02/

title: Palantir Results May Offer a Read on Corporate Demand for AI Software
content:
Palantir is scheduled to report results on Monday, giving investors another look at whether organizations are expanding their use of artificial-intelligence software beyond pilot projects. The company's performance is closely watched because its products are used by government agencies and commercial customers seeking to analyze data and coordinate operational decisions.

Investors are likely to focus on commercial customer growth, contract conversions, revenue guidance and the pace at which new AI tools become recurring business. Strong interest in AI does not automatically translate into immediate revenue: customers may test products, negotiate contracts or take time to integrate software into existing systems.

Palantir's report comes during a broader reassessment of AI valuations. Recent market declines have shown that investors increasingly want evidence of durable demand and cash generation rather than broad claims about the future size of the AI market.

The results could influence sentiment toward enterprise software and AI-linked stocks, but they should be considered alongside customer concentration, valuation, operating margins and management's outlook.

Source: Barron's, November 2, 2026 — https://www.barrons.com/articles/jobs-midterm-elections-apple-palantir-mcdonalds-moderna-stocks-4f608abf

title: AMD Earnings Could Test Investor Confidence in AI Processor Demand
content:
Advanced Micro Devices is due to report its quarterly results on Tuesday, November 3, in one of the week's most closely watched semiconductor updates. Investors will be looking for evidence that demand for data-center processors and accelerators is translating into revenue growth, stronger margins and credible forward guidance.

The market's expectations are high after a volatile period for chip shares. Recent declines have reflected concerns about the cost of AI infrastructure and whether suppliers can deliver enough performance and capacity to satisfy customers. AMD's outlook may help investors assess the competitive position of its data-center business and the balance between AI products and its other markets.

The company's earlier guidance pointed to third-quarter revenue of approximately $13 billion, plus or minus $300 million, according to Reuters coverage of the earnings calendar. That figure was guidance, not the final reported result.

Investors should pay close attention to segment performance, supply constraints, customer concentration and management's comments about the next quarter. Even strong revenue growth may not satisfy the market if expectations or margins are higher.

Source: Reuters, November 1, 2026 — https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/midterm-us-elections-earnings-jobs-data-loom-for-aiwary-stock-market-4920345

title: U.S. Midterm Elections Put Technology and Energy Policy Under the Microscope
content:
The November 3 U.S. midterm elections are taking place while investors are already debating the direction of technology, energy and financial regulation. Control of Congress can influence hearings, budget priorities and the prospects for legislation, although campaign proposals do not automatically become law.

Technology companies are watching discussions around artificial-intelligence oversight, data-center construction and electricity demand. Energy firms may be affected by permitting, infrastructure and climate policy, while banks and digital-asset businesses are monitoring the regulatory environment. Healthcare companies also face potential changes in oversight and federal spending priorities.

Reuters has identified the elections, corporate earnings and the October jobs report as major tests for investors this week. Market reactions may depend less on a single headline result than on whether the outcome changes expectations for future legislation and government spending.

Investors should separate confirmed policy decisions from campaign statements and speculative scenarios. The practical effects will depend on the final composition of Congress, committee priorities and the ability of lawmakers to reach agreements.

Source: Reuters, November 1, 2026 — https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/midterm-us-elections-earnings-jobs-data-loom-for-aiwary-stock-market-4920345

title: October U.S. Jobs Report Could Shape the Next Federal Reserve Debate
content:
The U.S. employment report for October is scheduled for Friday and is expected to be one of the week's most important economic releases. Investors will use the figures to assess hiring momentum, unemployment and wage trends at a time when the Federal Reserve is balancing economic resilience against persistent inflation risks.

A Reuters week-ahead report said economists were looking for payroll growth of about 62,000, following an increase of 29,000 in September, with unemployment expected to remain at 4.2%. These are forecasts rather than confirmed outcomes, and revisions to earlier months can also change the interpretation.

A stronger-than-expected report could reinforce the view that demand remains firm, potentially affecting bond yields and expectations for interest rates. A weaker report could raise concerns about slowing activity, although the inflation outlook would remain important to the Fed's decisions.

Investors should examine the details rather than focus on one headline number. Labor-force participation, average hourly earnings, hours worked and revisions can provide a fuller picture of employment conditions.

Source: Reuters, November 1, 2026 — https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/midterm-us-elections-earnings-jobs-data-loom-for-aiwary-stock-market-4920345

title: Manufacturing Data Offers a Fresh Check on the Health of U.S. Industry
content:
A new U.S. manufacturing survey is due on Monday, giving investors an updated view of factory activity, orders, employment and input prices. The Institute for Supply Management's October manufacturing index is among the economic releases being watched as markets assess whether business activity can remain resilient despite higher financing costs and trade uncertainty.

The headline purchasing managers' index is useful because it summarizes whether more surveyed companies report improving or deteriorating conditions. A reading above 50 generally indicates expansion, while a reading below 50 indicates contraction. The sub-indexes can be just as important: new orders may signal future demand, while prices paid can provide information about cost pressures.

Manufacturing data can influence several sectors at once, including industrial companies, transport operators, materials producers and banks. It can also affect bond markets if investors believe the report changes the outlook for growth or inflation.

The release should be interpreted alongside services activity, consumer spending and employment data. A single survey is not a complete measure of the U.S. economy, but it can help identify changes in business momentum.

Source: Hyper Stocks economic calendar, November 2, 2026 — https://terminal.hyperstocks.io/economic-calendar/2026-11-02

title: U.S. and Canada Restart Trade Talks as Businesses Watch Tariff Risks
content:
The United States and Canada have signaled renewed momentum in trade discussions after Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney described a recent conversation with U.S. President Donald Trump as constructive. Both sides said their teams would continue working toward a possible agreement in the coming weeks, but no final terms have been announced.

The dispute has involved tariffs and retaliatory measures affecting cross-border commerce. Businesses in autos, steel, agriculture, energy and manufacturing are particularly exposed because supply chains and production networks operate across the border. Uncertainty over duties can influence sourcing decisions, investment plans and prices paid by consumers.

The Associated Press reported that Trump referred to the possibility of a deal while Carney said negotiations would continue. The public comments indicate a change in tone, not a completed agreement. Any eventual deal would need specific terms and a process for implementation.

For investors, the next questions include whether tariff relief is negotiated, which industries are covered and how quickly businesses receive clarity. Until details are published, companies should continue to plan for policy uncertainty.

Source: Associated Press, November 2, 2026 — https://apnews.com/article/d0bfffc67ecdf22d9a5abffb2d26d848

title: Keystone XL Returns to the Trade Debate, but Major Questions Remain
content:
The Keystone XL pipeline has re-entered public discussion after President Donald Trump mentioned the project during comments about a possible U.S.-Canada trade agreement. The original project was canceled after a long regulatory and political dispute, and its future remains uncertain.

Reuters reported that the proposed concept would involve Canada paying for the pipeline, but the details of how a canceled project could proceed have not been established. The former developer, TC Energy, later separated its crude-pipeline business into South Bow, which is considering a different Prairie Connector proposal between Alberta and Wyoming and expects to decide in 2027 whether to proceed.

The issue matters because Canada sends more than 90% of its crude oil exports to the United States. Pipeline capacity can affect transportation costs, regional price differences and the ability of producers to move oil to refineries.

Investors should distinguish political statements from permits, financing, construction plans and binding commercial agreements. Any new route would face practical, regulatory and economic tests before it could affect oil flows.

Source: Reuters, November 1, 2026 — https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/canada-pm-carney-said-he-had-good-conversation-with-trump-trade-2026-11-01/

title: Oil Prices Retreat as Investors Assess Possible U.S.-Iran Diplomacy
content:
Oil prices fell sharply on Monday as traders assessed renewed diplomatic activity involving the United States and Iran. The decline followed a period of elevated prices and concerns about shipping security in the Gulf, showing how quickly geopolitical expectations can influence energy markets.

The Associated Press reported that U.S. and regional diplomatic efforts were being discussed in Qatar, while Reuters said oil fell more than 3% during the session. Reports of possible negotiations can reduce the immediate risk premium in crude prices, but they do not guarantee that shipping routes will reopen or that supply disruptions will end.

For energy companies, lower crude prices can reduce revenue for producers while potentially easing costs for airlines, transport operators and fuel-intensive manufacturers. Refiners and integrated oil companies may experience different effects depending on margins, inventories and contract structures.

The market will continue to monitor the progress of diplomacy, tanker movements, production decisions and inventory data. Price moves based on negotiations can reverse quickly if talks stall or security risks increase.

Source: Reuters, November 2, 2026 — https://www.reuters.com/world/china/global-markets-global-markets-2026-11-02/

title: Dollar Holds Steady as U.S. Election and Jobs Data Approach
content:
Currency markets began the week with traders cautious ahead of the U.S. midterm elections and a series of economic releases. The dollar was broadly steady as investors considered the possible effect of the vote on fiscal policy, trade relations and the balance of power in Congress.

Reuters reported that the dollar index was near 101.94 in early Asian trading on Monday. The euro was close to $1.1159, while sterling was little changed around $1.3387. These are market snapshots from the reported session and can change throughout the day.

The currency outlook is also linked to interest-rate expectations. The October employment report and other data may influence views about the Federal Reserve, while policy decisions in other major economies can shift relative yields and currency demand.

Investors should remember that exchange rates respond to several factors at once, including bond yields, growth expectations, political risk and safe-haven flows. A quiet session before a major event does not necessarily indicate that volatility has disappeared.

Source: Reuters, November 2, 2026 — https://www.marketscreener.com/news/dollar-rangebound-ahead-of-us-midterms-bitcoin-reels-from-crypto-heist-ce785fd8dd8ff523

title: Crypto Markets Weigh the Fallout From a Reported $6.3 Billion Binance Heist
content:
Digital-asset markets entered November under pressure after reports of a major security incident involving Binance. Reuters reported that bitcoin and ether were nursing losses following what it described as a record $6.3 billion heist at the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange.

A large exchange-related security event can affect confidence beyond the platform involved. Traders may reassess custody arrangements, withdrawal procedures, counterparty exposure and the safety of assets held with centralized service providers. The immediate effect can include higher volatility and shifts toward self-custody or other venues.

The reported incident also comes as investors face a busy week of macroeconomic events, including U.S. midterm elections, employment data and central-bank decisions in several countries. Broader risk appetite can influence crypto prices alongside industry-specific developments.

The full market impact depends on verified details about the incident, affected assets, recovery efforts and any regulatory response. Investors should avoid relying on unverified social-media claims and should assess exchange and wallet security independently.

Source: Reuters, November 2, 2026 — https://www.marketscreener.com/news/dollar-rangebound-ahead-of-us-midterms-bitcoin-reels-from-crypto-heist-ce785fd8dd8ff523

title: China's Factory Activity Slips Back Into Contraction in October
content:
China's official manufacturing activity weakened in October, adding another data point to the debate over domestic demand and the outlook for global trade. The National Bureau of Statistics reported that the official purchasing managers' index fell to 49.3 from 50.1 in September. A reading below 50 indicates contraction.

The Associated Press reported that new export orders and production sub-indexes also weakened. The data suggest that factories faced softer conditions after the previous month's return to expansion, although one monthly survey does not establish a lasting trend.

China's manufacturing performance matters to U.S. companies through supply chains, commodity demand and competition in export markets. A slowdown can weigh on industrial suppliers and raw-material producers, while changes in export pricing can affect manufacturers in other countries.

Investors will watch subsequent surveys, trade figures and policy announcements for evidence of whether authorities respond with additional support. The October reading is a warning about uneven momentum, not proof that China's economy is entering a broader downturn.

Source: Associated Press, November 2, 2026 — https://central.newschannelnebraska.com/story/370524189/ap-business-summarybrief-at-1230-am-est

title: Kioxia Forecast Miss Shows Investors Are Becoming More Discerning About AI
content:
Kioxia shares dropped sharply on Monday after the Japanese memory-chip maker issued a forecast that disappointed investors despite continuing demand for AI-related memory products. Business Insider reported that the company expected roughly flat revenue and operating profit in its December quarter, partly reflecting delays in data-center storage shipments and a product mix weighted toward lower-priced smartphone and PC chips.

The market reaction illustrates a more selective phase for AI-linked investments. Strong long-term demand does not prevent a share-price decline when near-term guidance falls short of expectations. Investors are increasingly comparing the timing of shipments, product mix, pricing and capacity commitments rather than treating all semiconductor companies as beneficiaries to the same degree.

Kioxia also indicated that memory supply could remain tight in 2027 and that planned capacity was sold out, according to the report. That outlook may support the longer-term industry narrative, but it does not remove quarterly execution risks.

The episode is a reminder that AI infrastructure spending creates opportunities across the supply chain while leaving individual companies exposed to delivery schedules and customer purchasing patterns.

Source: Business Insider, November 2, 2026 — https://www.businessinsider.com/another-chip-stock-selloff-shows-how-the-ai-trade-is-getting-pickier-2026-11

title: SK Hynix Gains Attention as Long-Term Memory Agreements Support AI Supply
content:
Memory-chip makers are attracting renewed attention as data-center operators seek reliable supplies for artificial-intelligence infrastructure. Business Insider reported that SK Hynix shares advanced after the company disclosed long-term customer agreements covering future memory production, while its rival Kioxia fell after issuing a weaker near-term forecast.

The contrast highlights the importance of product mix and contract visibility in the semiconductor industry. High-bandwidth memory and other advanced products are central to AI systems, but companies still need to manage production capacity, investment costs and delivery schedules. Long-term agreements can improve visibility, although they do not eliminate manufacturing or pricing risks.

Investors are also watching whether supply remains constrained into 2027 and how much of future production has already been committed. The balance between tight supply and new capacity will influence pricing power and capital spending across the memory market.

The diverging share reactions show why investors should assess each company's product portfolio, customer contracts and guidance rather than assume all memory suppliers will benefit equally from AI demand.

Source: Business Insider, November 2, 2026 — https://www.businessinsider.com/another-chip-stock-selloff-shows-how-the-ai-trade-is-getting-pickier-2026-11

title: About 135 S&P 500 Companies Are Set to Report in a Busy Earnings Week
content:
The first full week of November brings another heavy wave of U.S. corporate earnings. Barron's reported that about 135 S&P 500 companies are scheduled to release results, giving investors a broad look at technology, healthcare, consumer, industrial and financial businesses.

Apple and Palantir are among the companies reporting Monday, followed by AMD, Amgen and Pfizer on Tuesday. McDonald's and Qualcomm are among Wednesday's notable reports, while Airbnb is expected later in the week and Moderna is scheduled for Friday. Reporting dates and timing can change, so investors should confirm details with company investor-relations pages.

The breadth of the calendar matters because market performance depends on more than a handful of mega-cap technology names. Consumer companies can provide clues about household spending, healthcare firms can reveal demand and pricing trends, and industrial companies can offer insight into capital investment and order backlogs.

Investors should compare results with each company's guidance and the expectations already reflected in share prices. A company can report growth and still see its stock fall if investors expected even stronger performance.

Source: Barron's, November 2, 2026 — https://www.barrons.com/articles/jobs-midterm-elections-apple-palantir-mcdonalds-moderna-stocks-4f608abf

title: McDonald's Results Will Be Watched for Signs of Changing U.S. Consumer Spending
content:
McDonald's is among the major companies expected to report during the week, and its results may provide investors with another view of consumer demand. Restaurant operators are watched for comparable sales, customer traffic, average spending per visit and the balance between value promotions and menu pricing.

The broader restaurant industry faces a difficult equation when households are sensitive to food, fuel and housing costs. Lower-priced offers can help maintain visits, but heavy discounting may pressure margins. Price increases can support revenue per order but may encourage customers to visit less often or choose cheaper alternatives.

Barron's included McDonald's among the companies to watch in a week when about 135 S&P 500 firms are scheduled to report. Investors will likely compare its performance with other consumer-facing businesses to assess whether demand is broadening or weakening.

One company's results cannot represent every household or income group. Traffic trends, regional performance and management's outlook will help determine whether the company is gaining market share or simply benefiting from changes in pricing.

Source: Barron's, November 2, 2026 — https://www.barrons.com/articles/jobs-midterm-elections-apple-palantir-mcdonalds-moderna-stocks-4f608abf

title: Amgen and Pfizer Earnings Put Healthcare Demand and Drug Pipelines in Focus
content:
Healthcare investors are preparing for a busy reporting schedule, with Pfizer and Amgen among the companies due to release results during the week. Their updates will be watched for product demand, revenue mix, research spending and management commentary on the outlook for medicines and biotechnology.

For large drugmakers, quarterly performance can be shaped by product launches, competition, pricing, reimbursement decisions and the timing of clinical milestones. Investors also assess research and development programs because pipeline progress can influence expectations for future revenue, although clinical outcomes remain uncertain.

The reports arrive as markets look for areas of earnings resilience beyond the technology sector. Healthcare businesses may have different demand drivers from semiconductor and cloud companies, but they face their own regulatory, patent and development risks.

Investors should focus on company-specific guidance and product-level performance rather than assume that one strong or weak report signals a trend across the entire healthcare industry.

Source: Barron's, November 2, 2026 — https://www.barrons.com/articles/jobs-midterm-elections-apple-palantir-mcdonalds-moderna-stocks-4f608abf

title: Qualcomm Results Could Reveal How AI Features Are Affecting Smartphone Chips
content:
Qualcomm is among the technology companies scheduled to report later in the week, and investors will be looking for updates on smartphone chip demand, premium-device launches and the adoption of on-device artificial-intelligence features.

The smartphone market is important to Qualcomm's chipset business, while connectivity and automotive products provide additional sources of revenue. The investment question is whether new AI capabilities encourage consumers and manufacturers to upgrade devices, and whether those features support higher-value processors or stronger content per handset.

The current technology selloff has made investors more attentive to near-term sales and cash flow. Companies associated with AI may face scrutiny if the commercial benefits take longer to appear than the investment cycle. Qualcomm's guidance can help clarify demand conditions in parts of the mobile supply chain.

Investors should examine handset volumes, customer mix, licensing performance and management's outlook. AI-enabled devices may create opportunities, but the pace of consumer replacement cycles remains a key variable.

Source: Barron's, November 2, 2026 — https://www.barrons.com/articles/jobs-midterm-elections-apple-palantir-mcdonalds-moderna-stocks-4f608abf

title: Gold Recovers as Investors Rebalance Risk Ahead of a Data-Heavy Week
content:
Gold recovered some ground on Monday after a difficult October, as investors prepared for U.S. elections, corporate earnings and the October employment report. Reuters reported that bullion was up about 0.9% during the session after a steep decline in the previous month.

Gold can respond to changes in real interest rates, currency movements, geopolitical risk and demand for portfolio protection. When bond yields rise, the opportunity cost of holding a non-yielding asset can increase; when uncertainty rises or the dollar weakens, gold may receive support. These relationships are not automatic and can shift as investors rebalance positions.

The week's calendar includes major technology earnings and policy events that could move both Treasury yields and the dollar. Developments in the Middle East may also affect safe-haven demand and energy prices.

A one-day rebound does not establish a new trend. Investors will be watching inflation expectations, central-bank guidance and fund flows to understand whether gold's recent volatility is easing or continuing.

Source: Reuters, November 2, 2026 — https://www.reuters.com/world/china/global-markets-global-markets-2026-11-02/

title: Investors Reassess U.S. Technology Valuations After a Month of Heavy Selling
content:
A sharp decline in technology shares has prompted investors to reconsider how much they are willing to pay for companies tied to artificial intelligence and cloud infrastructure. Reuters reported that more than $2 trillion was erased from the Nasdaq 100's market value last month as concerns about AI spending and growth expectations intensified.

The move has created a debate about whether the selloff reflects a temporary reset in valuations or a deeper reassessment of expected returns. Deutsche Bank upgraded U.S. technology stocks on November 2, arguing that the recent decline had gone too far and that much of the AI-related risk was already reflected in share prices.

That view is one investment assessment, not a guarantee of a recovery. The market still needs evidence that corporate earnings, free cash flow and customer demand can support the valuations investors previously assigned to leading technology companies.

Investors should compare companies individually, including their balance sheets, recurring revenue, competitive positions and capital requirements. Broad sector labels can conceal major differences in business quality and financial risk.

Source: Reuters, November 2, 2026 — https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/deutsche-bank-upgrades-us-tech-says-selloff-has-gone-too-far-2026-11-02/
